label: paragraph_title
text: TRUE ECONOMY!

label: text
text: VIEWS OF CHANCELLOR OF EXCHEQUER

label: text
text: DIPARTIMENTAL SACRIFICE

label: text
text: (Rauter's Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: Leeds, Jan. 20.

label: text
text: “If the Government was supported in the economy scheme, which it has prepared, no addition to the burden of taxation will be necessary,” declared Mr. Winston (Lurchill, Chancellor of the Exchequer, speaking at the Leeds Chamber of Commerce, but if the economy scheme was pulled to pieces and whittled down, the bill must be paid).

label: text
text: He announced that when Parliament met an Economy Bill would be introduced covering the whole field of expenditure. Every Department would be asked to make sacrifices. He declared that the policy of true economy was not complete if it did, not provide for wise expenditure.

label: text
text: The Government's main constructive measure would be a great scheme of electrical development. "If this Island is to continue to support the present immense population it cannot afford to be behind any part of the world in scientific organisation and equipment. Science and goodwill are the only two horses strong enough to pull our waggon up the hill."

label: text
text: Mr. Churchill mentioned that the could subsidy would probably approximate £21,000,000; three-quarters off which would go in paying the wages of the miners.

label: paragraph_title
text: HOOVER CRITICISED.

label: text
text: HANDLING OF THE RUBBER SITUATION.

label: text
text: INCONSISTENCY EXPOSED:

label: text
text: Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: Sharp criticism of Mr. Herbert Hoover's handling of the rubber situation is voiced by the Demo-

label: text
text: cratic organ, "The World, contending that Mr. Hoover's actions throughout are" full of idiosyncrasies. He attacks the British trust, but seems to forget that he belongs to a Government that believes in protecting American trusts by the highest possible tariff. Similarly, he insists that he does not wish to advise retaliatory measures, but recently he expressed the view that public opinion would demand the American banks to refuse loans to Great Britain if the Stevenson Rubber Restriction Act remained in force.

label: paragraph_title
text: FOKKER MISSING.

label: text
text: FEARS FOR THE PLOT AND OBSERVER.

label: text
text: LOST IN SNOWSTORM?

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: Amsterdam, Jan '20.

label: text
text: Grave misgiving is felt regarding the fate of the pilot and observer of an Army Fokker, which left Schiphol yesterday for coastal defence practice.

label: text
text: It is feared that they got lost in a snowstorm.

label: text
text: The destroyer made a search in the sea, but it was fruitless.

label: paragraph_title
text: TOKYO FLIGHT.

label: text
text: DANISH MILITARY PROJECT FINALISING

label: text
text: DEPOTS AT KARACHI & BANGKOK.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Arrangements are being completed for a Danish military flight to Tokyo.

label: text
text: Spure parts are being despatched to Karachi, which will be one of three main depots for the service of the flight, the others being Bangkok and Tokyo.

label: paragraph_title
text: STRIKE THREAT.

label: text
text: FRENCH MINERS WANT MORE WAGES.

label: text
text: REFERENDUM TO BE TAKEN.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Scroace.)

label: text
text: The National Council of the Federation of French Mine Workers has adopted a resolution declaring that unless wages are increased by January 21, to compensate for the increased cost of living, a referendum will be taken on the question of a general strike of French miners.

label: paragraph_title
text: MORE FLOODS

label: text
text: FIVE INCHES OF RAIN

label: text
text: (Reuter's Sorvice.)

label: text
text: Unprecedented rains in the low-lying Portuguese territory between Umtall and Beira have resulted in serious floods, which have caused a complete suspension of train, muil, and telegraphic services between Rhodesia and Beira.

label: text
text: Many natives have been drowned. Others, took refuge in trees and have been brought to Beira by motor boats.

label: text
text: The average rainfall in the district yesterday was five inches.

label: paragraph_title
text: "MERE BANDITRY."

label: text
text: MURDERS OF BOLSHEVIST OFFICIALS.

label: text
text: MOSCOW'S VERSION.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: A semi-official version of the murders in the Bobruisk district states that they were mere banditry and had no political significance.

label: text
text: Moscow, January 20.

label: text
text: [A Rign message of January 15 stated:—It is reported that much unrest prevails among the peasantry in various parts of Soviet Russia, particularly in the Ukraine and White Russia, where armed anti-Bolsheviks are active. Murders of over-zealous Communist officials are reported, chiefly in the Bobruisk district, where the militia and local authorities are alleged to have refused to act against the rebels, and are even co-operating with them.]

label: paragraph_title
text: MEXICO'S LAWS.

label: text
text: POSITION OF THE UNITED STATES

label: text
text: STATE SECRETARY SPEAKS OUT.

label: text
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text:
Mr. Kellogg, Secretary of State; in a formal statement said that a position of the United States in regard to the Mexican Land and Petroleum Laws was that they contained provisions "plainly retroactive and confiscatory in their effect."
He added that in the absence of a reply from the Mexican Government to the American representations on the subject, delivered on January 9, he was not disposed to comment further.
REPLY RECEIVED: Mexico City, Jan. 20.
The United States Ambassador has received from the Mexican Foreign Office a reply to his recent Note protesting against retroactive legislation, but declines to

text: WILLING TO PAY.

label: text
text: FRENCH DEBT TO UNITED STATES.

label: text
text: COOLIDGE NEEDN'T WORRY.

label: text
text: (Reuler's American Series):

label: text
text: M. Henry Berenger, the new French Ambassador, told President Coolidge that Finance is resolved to settle her war debts as promptly and fully as her present and future possibilities would allow.

label: text
text: Knocked down by a tram car at Kennedy Town yesterday, a Chinese coolie was taken to hospital yesterday with injuries to his face and arms.

label: text
text: The Scotsman away on his annual vacation was head over heels in love with a certain young "girl left behind him." At last he could stand the suspense no longer, and, going to the telegraph office, he at once sent off a telegram asking her if she would marry him. That happened in the morning, and he spent the entire day in the office waiting for a reply. That night a call came through accepting him.

label: text
text: "If I were you," said the operator, when at last he was leaving. "I should think twice before I'd marry a girl who kept me waiting all day long for an answer.

label: text
text: “Na, na,” retorted the Scot. “The girl who waits for the reduced night rates is the lass for me.”—Los Angeles “Times.”

label: paragraph_title
text: BRITISH TRIUMPH.

label: text
text: BIGGEST DAM IN THE WORLD.

label: text
text: SOUDA N'S FUTURE ASSURED

label: paragraph_title
text: (Router's Service)

label: text
text: London, January 20:

label: text
text: The Makwar dam, which Lord Lloyd will officially inaugurate on Thursday is a triumph of British engineering

label: text
text: The preparatory work "was started in 1914, stopped by the war, and resumed after the war when a loan of three million sterling, previously guaranteed by the British Treasury for the construction was doubled.

label: text
text: The dam and the canalisation for the big irrigation scheme which is ultimately intended to irrigate three million acres, was completed by Messrs. Pearson & Son in July last year.

label: text
text: In the first season 80,000 acres of cotton were irrigated compared with 20,000 acres under the old pumping scheme.

label: text
text: Two Miles Long.

label: text
text: In the first season 800,000 acres of cotton were irrigated, compared with 20,000 acres under the old pumping scheme.

label: text
text: The dam is nearly two miles long, with a maximum height of 128 feet. Nearly a million tons of masonry were used. The reservoir formed above the dam will be a lake 30 miles long.

label: text
text: The total length of the main canal will be 70 miles and its branches 558 miles.

label: text
text: Twenty thousand workmen were employed on the dam, along which a road and railway run. The latter will be eventually extended to Kassala.

label: text
text: A clergyman was having tea with some new parishoners. On the sideboard were some cut-glass decanters filled with what looked like whisky and various other spirits.

label: text
text:
"My friend," said the curate to his host, "you should avoid even the appearance of evil. I do not say that you drink, but ___"
"Why, they're only filled with furniture polish, Mr. Marsh and floor stain. It's the decanters that I like—they look so pretty."
"Exactly," said the curate. "I repeat, avoid even the appearance of evil. I took a drink from the

label: text
text: repeat, avoid even the appearance of evil. I took a drink from the big one in the middle."
